flows.name: Visit landing page
flows.goal: Understand what Studio Hub does and choose how to start.

steps.userAction: The visitor arrives at the landing page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows what Studio Hub is for the solo designer, how clients, projects, tasks and bookings work together, and how to sign in, create an account or open the public booking page.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to start sign-in, sign-up or open the public booking page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website starts the chosen entry and shows the sign-in screen, the sign-up screen or the public booking page.

flows.outcome: Nothing is stored; the visitor knows how to sign in, sign up or reach the booking page.

flows.name: Sign up

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty sign-up screen asking for account email and account password.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the account email and password and submits.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the account, signs the freelancer in and shows the private home screen with the three starter session types ready.

alternatives.condition: The account email is missing or not an email, or the account password is shorter than 8 characters.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the fields, keeps what was typed and explains how to fix them.

alternatives.condition: Saving fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The account email is already registered.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says an account with that email already exists and offers to sign in instead.

alternatives.condition: The visitor cancels.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is saved; the website shows the landing page as it was.

flows.outcome: Account is created and the freelancer is signed in; a refresh still shows the private home.

flows.name: Sign in

steps.userAction: The freelancer chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty sign-in screen asking for account email and account password.

steps.userAction: The freelancer enters the account email and password and submits.
steps.websiteResponse: The website signs the freelancer in and shows the private home screen with today's sessions, follow-ups and overdue tasks.

alternatives.condition: The account email is missing or not an email, or the account password is missing.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks the fields, keeps what was typed and explains how to fix them.

alternatives.condition: Signing in fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The email and password do not match an account.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the details were not recognised, keeps the email and offers to retry or sign up.

alternatives.condition: The visitor cancels.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing changes; the website shows the landing page as it was.

flows.outcome: Freelancer is signed in and sees the home screen; a refresh stays signed in.

flows.name: Sign out

steps.userAction: The freelancer chooses to sign out.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks to confirm leaving the workspace.

steps.userAction: The freelancer confirms leaving.
steps.websiteResponse: The website ends the session and shows the public landing page with private data hidden.

alternatives.condition: The freelancer cancels.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing changes; the website shows the home screen as it was and the freelancer stays signed in.

alternatives.condition: Signing out fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the freelancer signed in and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: Freelancer is signed out; a refresh shows the landing page and private data stays hidden until sign-in.

flows.name: See home for today
flows.goal: Start the day from today's sessions, this week's follow-ups and overdue tasks.

steps.userAction: The freelancer opens home.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows today's sessions with times and bookings, follow-ups due this week with overdue first, and overdue tasks highlighted.

steps.userAction: The freelancer chooses a session, client or task to open.
steps.websiteResponse: The website opens the chosen session, client or task with its details.

alternatives.condition: There are no sessions today, no follow-ups due this week and no overdue tasks.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows each list as empty with guidance to add clients, projects and tasks and to set availability so sessions can be booked.

alternatives.condition: The chosen session, client or task is no longer there.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says it is no longer available and shows the home lists as they are now.

flows.outcome: Nothing is changed; a refresh still shows the same three lists for today.

flows.name: Browse clients

steps.userAction: The freelancer opens the clients list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows every client with status and next follow-up date ordered with overdue follow-ups first.

alternatives.condition: The client is no longer there.

flows.outcome: Nothing is changed; a refresh shows the same ordered client list.

alternatives.condition: Saving fails.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website keeps the values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: Saving fails.

assumptions.text: Client emails are unique per freelancer case-insensitively; the client form rejects a duplicate email so booking auto-match stays reliable.
Follow-ups due this week means follow-up date is today or within the next 7 calendar days, plus all overdue follow-ups not yet marked done.
A project's open task count counts tasks whose status is not Done (To do plus In progress).

Weekly availability is a single start-to-end time window applied to each selected weekday; open slots regenerate for the next 14 days after every availability or session-type change, excluding past times.

A new freelancer workspace starts with the three named session types already present: 30min discovery free 1 seat, 60min design review 4000 1 seat, 120min Figma workshop 2500 8 seats, all editable and deletable with prices shown as text only.
A booking that creates a new Lead client fills name and email from the booking, leaves company empty and stores a profile noting it was auto-created from booking.
Each booking gets a unique per-booking cancellation link that shows booking details without sign-in; opening it after cancellation shows a cancelled state.

questions.question: Should a freelancer be prevented from creating two clients with the same email?
questions.whyItMatters: Changes booking auto-match reliability and whether bookings can land under the wrong client
questions.defaultAnswer: Yes, emails must be unique per freelancer case-insensitively and the form rejects duplicates

questions.question: In which time zone should availability windows and session times be shown to bookers?
questions.whyItMatters: Changes what slot times mean and whether bookings happen at the expected hour
questions.defaultAnswer: Show all times in the freelancer's local browser time zone for both freelancer and bookers
